content.title: About
content.content: Sponge cake is a light, airy pastry typically made from eggs, sugar, flour, and a small amount of fat. It serves as a base for many desserts, can be soaked with syrup, and topped with cream, fruit, or glaze.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sponge cake originated in Europe in the 19th century as a lighter alternative to heavy pies.
Traditional French génoise relies solely on the volume of beaten eggs, without any leavening agents.
In Japan, "sporki" – sponge roll cakes covered with sweet glaze – are a popular treat.
Sponge layers are often used in layered cakes, each layer being brushed with different syrups.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Sponge cake provides carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with energy.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Classic recipes contain little butter, making it less calorie‑dense than many other cakes.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The porous structure aids digestion, especially for those with mild gastrointestinal issues.

items.title: Egg or gluten allergy
items.content: Sponge cake contains eggs and wheat flour, which can trigger reactions in allergic individuals.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: The high sugar and simple carbohydrate content may cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sponge cake can be enjoyed on its own, sliced and served with berry sauce, used as a base for layered cakes, roulades, panna cotta, or simply toasted and dusted with powdered sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sponge cake in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, keep it in the refrigerator or freeze it, wrapped tightly in plastic film.

chicken-and-vegetable-entree-with-noodle.title: Chicken and vegetable entree with noodles and cream sauce, frozen meal

content.title: About
content.content: This ready‑to‑heat frozen meal contains pieces of chicken breast, mixed vegetables (carrot, broccoli, bell pepper), noodles and a smooth cream sauce. It is designed for quick preparation in a microwave or on the stovetop.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The meal is engineered for convenience: only 3‑5 minutes of heating are needed.
The cream sauce is made from dairy and vegetable oils, giving it a velvety texture.
The noodles are typically wheat‑based, which remain firm after freezing.
Chicken used is usually skin‑less, reducing the fat content.
This product is often part of the “quick lunch” range in supermarkets.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Chicken breast provides high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish contains vitamin B6 and niacin, which support metabolic processes.

items.title: Vegetable‑derived fiber
items.content: Broccoli, carrot and bell pepper add dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Calcium from cream sauce
items.content: The cream sauce contributes a modest amount of calcium, beneficial for bone health.

items.title: Balanced energy
items.content: The meal provides a moderate calorie count suitable for a quick, satisfying lunch.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The cream sauce contains milk, which can trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces often have added salt; individuals monitoring sodium intake should be aware of portion size.

items.title: Need for thorough heating
items.content: Insufficient heating may leave cold spots where bacteria could survive; follow heating instructions carefully.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The noodles are wheat‑based, making the product unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the frozen meal in the microwave (about 3‑4 minutes) or on the stovetop, stirring until evenly hot. If the sauce becomes too thick, add a splash of water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product frozen at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed, consume immediately and do not store at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
